about.title: Santa Clarita Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Santa Clarita is the result of someone else's carelessness, the people left behind carry more than grief. Bills arrive. A paycheck stops. A parent who drove the kids down McBean Parkway every morning is suddenly gone. Los Angeles County records show 14 traffic deaths in Santa Clarita in 2025, a year that also saw 706 injury collisions across the city. Public records list Soledad Canyon Road, Sierra Highway and Bouquet Canyon Road among the corridors with the highest collision counts. Not every fatal event involves a car, of course. Falls, defective products, workplace incidents and medical errors can also give rise to a wrongful death claim under California law. LawProactive exists to take one task off your list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Santa Clarita families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we make the introduction; the attorney explains your options.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can tell you quickly where your family stands.

items.title: Awareness of the Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims involving a government entity face a much shorter window. Connecting early protects that timeline.

items.title: A Full Picture of Recoverable Losses
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California law recognizes lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can help you understand what may apply to your family.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Sierra Highway. Does it matter who maintains the road?
items.answer: It can. If a claim involves a public agency, such as the City of Santa Clarita, Los Angeles County or a state agency, California requires a formal government claim within a much shorter period than the usual two years. Missing that step can end a case before it begins. This is one reason to speak with an attorney soon after a death, even while you are still grieving.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a separate civil action with its own deadline, and it does not depend on a criminal conviction. The two proceedings can move forward at the same time. An attorney can explain how evidence from the criminal case may still be useful to your civil claim.

items.question: I was not married to my partner. Can I still bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California gives first priority to a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and to children. Certain other people who were financially dependent on the person who died may also have standing in some situations. Because eligibility depends on your specific relationship and circumstances, an independent attorney can review your situation and tell you whether you qualify.
